newsitem.title: UK: British Gas may escape tough price cuts.
newsitem.headline: British Gas may escape tough price cuts.

text.p: British Gas Plc may escape the tough price cuts that industry regulator Ofgas wants to impose on its TransCo pipeline operation, according to a report in the Sunday Times newspaper.

The paper said Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission may favour a more lenient policy than Ofgas, which had demanded a price cut of 20 percent followed by price rises of 2.5 percentage points below inflation for the next four years.

British Gas is in the throes of demerging its TransCo gas distribution arm from its exploration and production arm. It rejected the Ofgas price proposals last year, triggering the reference to the MMC.
It said the Ofgas demands, if implemented, could lead to a two-thirds cut in British Gas's dividend, but it gave no indication of the pricing policy that it believed the MMC may favour.

However the paper said any relief for shareholders from the MMC would be tempered by renewed fears over a so-called "windfall tax", planned by the opposition Labour Party if it wins an election that must be held by May.

It said a negative report from Scottish Amicable Investment Managers said British Gas would be one of the utilities hardest hit by the tax, which could be converted from a one-off into an ongoing tax. No one at Ofgas or British Gas was available for comment.
